default.description: Grants the page almost nothing, and that is a claim about the whole API surface rather than about the empty list it used to hold. Everything this shell does apart from one thing - navigating the window, setting its title, toggling screenshot protection - is driven from Rust, so the web layer needs no API surface. The one exception is the update prompt's answer, below. Capabilities attach to a window label rather than to an origin, so `remote.urls` below is what pins the grant to one host: `WHISPERNET_URL` can point this shell at a different origin, and without the entry the new origin would fall outside `local: true`, every `set_update_consent` call would be rejected, and the updater would download, verify and unpack an update that could then never install. Naming the host means an operator override gets a clearly broken update flow instead of a silent one, and any new host has to be added here deliberately - which is the point of naming it.
